summary: Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of London around 1974–1978 and served as a professor at SOAS University of London from approximately 1982 to 2011.
Taeseung Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University from around 1982 to 1991 and studied under Jikido Takasaki through 1991.
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Hong Kong from around 1993 to 1998, earning a PhD under doctoral supervisor Ming-Wood Liu.

Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (~1994–1998). He became an adjunct professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994) and began teaching at Loyola University Chicago (~2011).

Taiji Kuroda worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University around 1975–1978 and served as an assistant professor (助教授) at Osaka Gakuin University and Osaka Gakuin College.

Taijun Inokuchi specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts as a committee member (委員) at Ryukoku University in 1987 and as representative (代表者) of The Society for the History of Buddhism.

Taiken Kimura was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Japan Women's University (~1912–1923) and as assistant professor (助教授) at the University of Tokyo (1908–1930).
Taiken Kyuma is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Vienna (~1995–1999) and served as an associate professor at Mie University from around 2004 to 2008.
Taiken Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. He later held an assistant professor (助教授) post at Aichi Gakuin University.
Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University from around 2011 to 2016. Mibu also served as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University.

Taiko Yamasaki worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Koyasan University (~1949–1953) under Bokushō Kanayama, later serving in posts at Koyasan University and Shuchiin University (~1997–2005).

Tainori Tanigawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Koyasan University (~1974–1979) and earned a Ph.D. from Toyo University by 1994, serving as an assistant professor (助教授) at Koyasan University around 1983.
Taion Satomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from around 1930 to 1933. He later held a position as a professor (教授) at Minobusan Junior College.

Tairyo Makita specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studying at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1957–1976), president of Saitama Institute of Technology (~1984–1990), and held a post at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.
Taitaka Tsunoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Tsunoda served as a lecturer (講師) at Komazawa Junior College from around 1992 to 1995 and became a professor at Komazawa University around 1995.
Taisei Iwata specialized in Buddhist studies, studying under Shinjo Suguro. Iwata held positions as a lecturer (講師) at Rissho University and as a professor (教授) at Otani University.

Taishu Tagami specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts as professor (教授) at Komazawa University (~1970–2006) and concurrent lecturer (講師(兼任)) at the Eastern Institute.
Taishun Mibu worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University (~1934–1937) and later served there as library director (図書館長) from around 1948 to 1980.

Taitetsu Unno was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1968). He was a professor at Smith College from around 1971 to 1998.

Taixu was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Jichan in 1907. He founded several institutes, including the Minnan Buddhist Institute (serving as its leader in 1927), the Wuchang Buddhist Institute, Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute, and Tianning Buddhist College.
